label: rem:unstable-atom-decay-phase
title: Decay channel, phase boundary, and phase-interior shortcut
html:
Remark. Decay channel, phase boundary, and phase-interior shortcut

Decay channel. An unstable atom must drop to a lower confinement level. It either adjoins a higher-energy operator (which then becomes available, raising \ell and enlarging the ILP search space) or transitions to a different atom-knot K' at the same or lower level. The decay product is determined by:

  1. Identifying the violated constraint \gamma^* = \arg\min_\gamma (\mathrm{G}(q) x)_\gamma over all ILP-attempted x. This is the constraint with the smallest shadow price contribution.
  2. Identifying the decay channel as the operator e_{\lambda^*} whose contribution to \gamma^* is most negative. This is the operator that fails to satisfy Frobenius positivity.
  3. Obtaining the daughter atom K' by removing e_{\lambda^*} from the normal form and re-running the ILP on the reduced primitive set.

This matches the classical \beta-decay picture. An unstable nucleus emits the operator that violates positivity, and the daughter has fewer constraints.

Phase boundary. An atom that is stable at q_1 and unstable at q_2 necessarily has a boundary point q^* \in [q_1, q_2] where the relevant shadow price vanishes:

  E(\lambda^*, q^*)
  \;=\;
  |y_{\lambda^*}(q^*)|
  \;=\;
  0.

Crossing q^* is a categorical phase transition. The operator \lambda^* disappears from the LP-dual basis, the filtration restructures, and the ILP feasibility flips. This is the operator-theoretic origin of the empirical observation that isotope stability changes abruptly between adjacent A values (e.g. {}^{12}\mathrm{C} is stable, but {}^{14}\mathrm{C} is unstable).

Computational shortcut (phase interior). For an atom K deep inside a phase (i.e. \min_\lambda |u_\lambda(q)| \gg 0 at the operating q), the ILP is strictly feasible with a wide margin. The per-generator \hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}} values (mass-endomorphism-tower) are locally constant in q. They can be interpolated linearly between magic-number anchors without re-running the full Wedderburn decomposition. We only need exact per-generator extraction at phase boundaries (where a shadow price vanishes). This justifies computing exact tower data only at magic configurations and interpolating elsewhere.
